traceability.notes:
All functional acceptance criteria in docs/stories/010.3-DEV-MIGRATE-TO-SUPPORTS.story.md are implemented and verified by tests:
- Optional Warning / Configurable Enforcement (REQ-OPTIONAL-WARNING, REQ-CONFIG-SEVERITY): The rule is defined as a suggestion, is not included in the recommended/strict presets, and is controlled entirely via ESLint severity (off/warn/error). Tests in tests/rules/prefer-implements-annotation.test.ts confirm it is disabled by default in both presets and can be configured with warn/error severities.
- Auto-fix Support & Single Story Conversion (REQ-AUTO-FIX, REQ-SINGLE-STORY-FIX): The rule implements conservative auto-fix logic via buildImplementsAutoFix and applyImplementsReplacement, which converts a single @story with one or multiple simple @req lines into a single @supports line while removing the originals. Tests assert correct output for both single-req and multi-req cases.
- Multi-story Detection / Mixed Usage (REQ-MULTI-STORY-DETECT): The implementation detects mixed @story/@req/@supports comments and multiple distinct @story paths, reporting cannotAutoFix with an explicit reason or multiStoryDetected, respectively. Tests cover both scenarios and validate the messages.
- Preserve Order and Formatting (REQ-PRESERVE-FORMAT): The fixer reconstructs the comment in-place, replacing only the @story line with a @supports line, removing @req lines, and preserving all other lines (description, @param, @returns, etc.) in their original order and using the original indentation and leading `*` prefix. This matches the story’s requirement that @supports sit after the description and before parameter tags.
- Both Formats Valid / Backward Compatibility (REQ-BACKWARD-COMP-VALIDATION): When the rule is disabled (the default in presets), it has no effect. Even when enabled, processComment exits early if a comment has only @story, only @req, or only @supports, meaning legacy annotations still pass. The tests’ valid cases explicitly exercise and confirm that behavior.
- Valid Output (REQ-VALID-OUTPUT): Auto-fix is intentionally conservative—only simple single-story, single-line @story and @req forms are transformed; any complex or ambiguous case causes the fixer to bail and emit diagnostics without changing code. This design ensures that all generated @supports lines conform to the existing validation rules.
- Documentation: There is a dedicated rule doc (docs/rules/prefer-implements-annotation.md), a user-facing migration guide (user-docs/migration-guide.md), and README entries describing the optional migration rule, auto-fix behavior, and opt-in configuration. These collectively satisfy the documentation acceptance criterion.
All relevant Jest tests for this story pass as part of the full test suite. There is a minor traceability naming inconsistency in docs/rules/prefer-implements-annotation.md (it references MIGRATE-TO-IMPLEMENTS rather than MIGRATE-TO-SUPPORTS), but this does not affect behavior and does not undermine satisfaction of the story’s functional and documentation acceptance criteria. Overall, the story is fully implemented and verified.
